issues.description: The file is named 'README' without a standard extension (.md or .txt). This reduces IDE support, syntax highlighting, and automated tooling integration.

issues.description: The file does not end with a newline character. According to POSIX standards, text files should end with a newline character.
issues.suggestion: Add a newline character at the end of the file. Most modern code editors can be configured to automatically add trailing newlines on save. This prevents Git warnings and issues with command-line utilities.

recommendations.description: Replace the vague placeholder text 'Changes the file' with meaningful project documentation. The README should explain what the project is, how to use it, and provide installation instructions. This will significantly improve the repository's professionalism and usability.

Add standard README sections including project title as a header, description, installation instructions, usage examples, and license information. Follow common Markdown README conventions with proper header formatting (e.g., '# Hello World').

Rename the file from 'README' to 'README.md' to enable better IDE support, syntax highlighting, GitHub rendering, and automated tooling integration. This is a standard convention for Markdown documentation.

Add a newline character at the end of the file to comply with POSIX text file standards. This prevents Git warnings ('No newline at end of file') and ensures compatibility with command-line text processing tools.

Consider implementing documentation quality checks in the CI/CD pipeline, such as markdownlint for syntax validation, spell-checking, and content quality tests. While not critical for this simple change, these would improve documentation standards for future contributions.
